_readme: Every entry is one node in the tree. To add a food: copy an entry, give it a unique id, set parent to an existing id, and fill in the fields. Ranks in order: domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species, variety. A node may skip ranks.

nodes.short: Everything that can be eaten or drunk. Gas station sushi is included under protest.

nodes.trait: Exists to make other food better, never the star
nodes.short: Seasonings, sauces, dips and spreads. Checked first, because ketchup will try to claim it is a meal.
Tomato-based supporting cast. Banned from Chicago-style specimens by local statute.
A seasoning. Salting a steak does not make the steak a constructed food; the salt is merely visiting.
Made by fermentation and chemically the same glutamate found in tomatoes. Supporting cast with an unfair reputation.
Anchovy, garlic, parmesan and egg, emulsified. Supporting cast in the chicken Caesar salad.
Supporting cast for sushi and sashimi. Never the star, however much is poured.

nodes.trait: Has a beverage role: hydrate, refresh, stimulate or intoxicate
nodes.short: Drinks, sorted by how they were made: ready-made by nature, pressed, steeped, dissolved, fermented, or mixed from other drinks. A milkshake is a dessert wearing a straw, and lives in Constructa.

nodes.trait: Comes out of nature ready to drink
nodes.short: Nothing was squeezed, steeped, dissolved or fermented. Filtering and pasteurizing do not count.
Water, with or without bubbles.
Flat by design.
Water.
The control group.
The baseline every other drink is measured against. Tap or bottled is a vessel question, and the vessel does not count.
Bubbles. The only thing separating these from their still relatives.
Water that fizzes.
Seltzer, club soda, mineral water with bubbles.
Water with bubbles. One order away from tap water, and it will not let you forget it.
From an animal, as nature intended. Plant milks are elsewhere, and they know why.
Flat by design.
Species sorted by animal.
Fat percentage makes a variety, not a species.
The default milk. Whole, 2% and skim are varieties: you still order it as milk.
Nothing removed.
Most of the fat removed. Most of the joy, some argue.
A different animal, so a different species of milk.
Rarely drunk, frequently turned into cheese.

nodes.trait: Squeezed, pressed or strained from a plant
nodes.short: Juices and plant milks: the liquid was already inside the plant, or close to it.
Mostly squeezed fruit by volume. Lemonade fails this test.
Flat by design.
Oranges, grapefruit and relatives.
The breakfast table genus.
Squeezed oranges. Pulp is a variety question the Board refuses to take up.
Pressed orchard fruit.
Pressed apples.
Pressed apples. Once fermented it becomes cider and leaves for Fermentata.

nodes.trait: Strained from grains, nuts or beans, and sold as milk
nodes.short: Pressed and strained from a plant, so not milk. Oat milk is, technically, oat juice. Same idea as Pseudosandwichae, different material.
Flat by design.

nodes.trait: A plant soaked, blended and strained
nodes.short: The family that drew the strongest letters.
Oat, almond, soy and whatever comes next.
Not milk. Oats soaked, blended and strained: oat juice with excellent marketing.
Not milk. Almonds, water and confidence.
Not milk. Soybeans soaked, ground and strained.

nodes.trait: Steeped in hot water, then the solids removed
nodes.short: Coffee and tea: the flavor was pulled out of something that is then thrown away.
Coffee.
Flat by design.
The family most responsible for this website existing past midnight.
Hot water drips or soaks through ground beans, helped only by gravity and patience.
Add-ins make varieties, not new species: you still order it as coffee. A latte is ordered by a different name, so it is a separate species.
Coffee as intended.
Cream and sugar, by New York definition. Listing a variety is not an endorsement of it.
Coffee made under pressure, named for the tan foam on top. Its own line on every café menu.
Hot water forced through finely packed grounds under pressure, in about 25 seconds. Ordered by its own name, so its own species.
nodes.long: Not Expressa. In Expressa the food itself gets squeezed (an orange, an oat). Here the beans sit still and the water is pushed through them, which is steeping in a hurry. Order and family stand: no bubbles (crema is foam, not carbonation), and it is still built around the coffee bean.

nodes.short: Two shots. More of the same thing is a variety.
A short pull: less water, same beans. Has its own name, still the same drink.
A long pull: more water through the same puck. Not an Americano, which adds water afterward.
Tea.
Flat by design.
Black, green and everything between.
Tea from the tea plant. Herbal teas would need a family of their own.
Leaves steeped in hot water. Additions make varieties: you still order it as tea.
Strong black tea with a splash of milk. Steeping time is a matter of national security.
Iced tea sweetened past the point of debate. Southern variety; served by the gallon.
Sugar, flavor, salts or syrup dissolved into water. Where the syrup meets the water, in a factory or a fountain, does not matter.

nodes.trait: Sugar and flavor dissolved in water
nodes.short: Soda and lemonade.
Bubbles. The only thing separating these from their still relatives.
Caramel-colored, kola-flavored, endlessly argued over.
The brown sodas.
Can, bottle or 2-liter: same species. The vessel does not count.
Sweetened without sugar. Still ordered as a cola.
Cola with cherry. A variety, not a new species.
Syrup and carbonated water combined at the moment of pouring. Same species as the can; recognized as a variety in honor of everyone who insists the fast-food version tastes better.
The clear sodas.
Clear and citrusy.
Clear citrus soda.
Flat by design.
Mostly water by volume, which is why it is not juice.
The front-yard stand genus.
Not juice. Mostly water with sugar and some lemon juice dissolved in, so it sits with soda, not orange juice.

nodes.trait: Salts and sugar dissolved for exercise
nodes.short: Water with electrolytes. The color is not a flavor.
Flat by design.
Engineered for sweat replacement.
Sold by color.
Salts and sugar dissolved in water. Its purpose is hydration, but the Board sorts drinks by how they are made, not why.
Yeast or bacteria turned sugar into something more interesting.
Beer. Sometimes called liquid bread; the Board notes that liquid bread is still not a sandwich.
Bubbles. The only thing separating these from their still relatives.
Most beer.
Fermented grain, drunk to unwind.
A drink, not a food: its beverage role wins even though it is assembled from grain, hops, yeast and water.
Sold by the 30-rack. Pale, cold and faintly reminiscent of the stadium it was advertised in.
Brewed in a former auto-body shop and served in a stemmed glass. Named after a local landmark or the brewer's dog. Tasting notes available on request, and also without request.
Wine and cider.
Flat by design.
Wine as most people mean it.
Red, white and the arguments between.
Fermented with the grape skins on.
Fermented with the skins removed.
Bubbles. The only thing separating these from their still relatives.
One order away from still wine.
Wine that fizzes.
Wine with bubbles. Champagne is a regional variety, as the French will remind you.
Two drinks combined into a new one with its own name: lattes, cocktails, an Arnold Palmer.
Lattes and their relatives.
Flat by design.
Mostly milk, ordered as coffee.
Lattes, cappuccinos, flat whites.
Not coffee. Espresso and steamed milk, two finished drinks mixed into one with its own name. Mostly milk by volume.

nodes.common: One food, bossed around but recognizable
nodes.trait: Could the original pick it out of a police lineup?
nodes.short: A single food, dried, salted, pickled or grilled. A cucumber can identify a pickle; flour cannot identify toast.
One food, grilled. The salt and pepper on top belong to Condimenta; the cow would still recognize it.
A grape with life experience.
Passes the police lineup test: a cucumber would recognize it instantly.
Raw tuna, sliced. One food, still recognizable: the tuna would pick it out of a lineup. The soy sauce and wasabi are Condimenta. Not sushi, because there is no rice.

nodes.trait: The originals can't recognize themselves, or several foods share the job
nodes.short: Where nearly every argument happens. Sorted into phyla by what holds the food together.

nodes.trait: Ingredients fused into one new mass
nodes.short: The building materials: breads, pastas, sausages and cheeses.
Bread in every form: loaves, buns, rolls, tortillas, fried shells, batter. The only material that makes a sandwich.
Bread, toasted. Still constructed, because bread was built from flour, water and yeast.

nodes.trait: Dough cooked in water or steam
nodes.short: Pasta, noodles, dumpling wrappers and steamed buns. Cooked wet, so not bread.

nodes.trait: Meat fused into a new shape
nodes.short: Sausages, franks and meatballs. The frank alone lives here; in a bun it graduates to Involucra.
Cheese.

nodes.trait: Seasoned rice pressed into one mass
nodes.short: Sushi rice: vinegared, seasoned and packed until the grains act as one mass. Not bread, because the grain was never ground into dough. Loose steamed rice does not qualify.

nodes.trait: Fat-rich dough baked into a crust
nodes.short: Shortcrust and puff pastry. Baked like bread, but built from fat as much as flour, which makes it its own material.

nodes.trait: The food is its own plate
nodes.short: A container food holds a filling. What the container is made of decides the class: bread, dough, rice, pastry or a whole food.

nodes.trait: A filling held between bread: bread on opposite sides of the filling
nodes.short: The class this entire website exists to defend. A sandwich is a filling between bread, and only bread qualifies; its cousins in other materials have classes of their own. Sandwiches are sorted by their bread all the way down. The filling is a passenger and is only identified at genus.

nodes.trait: Slices taken from a larger loaf
nodes.short: The classic arrangement your opponents think is the only kind. The bread was a loaf before it was a sandwich.

nodes.trait: Two or more slices cut from a loaf
nodes.short: Undisputed by everyone, which makes them boring.
Cold cuts, bacon, lettuce, whatever fits. The genus every other sandwich is measured against.
The type specimen. Nobody has ever filed an appeal.

nodes.trait: One whole roll, bun, tortilla or coating per sandwich, however it is cut, hinged, folded or sealed
nodes.short: Home of the hot dog, the burger, the sub, the taco and the burrito. The bread was made for this sandwich and nothing else.
nodes.long: A hamburger bun is cut all the way through and a hot dog bun is hinged; both are whole buns, so both are here. Cutting a roll in half before building the sandwich is the same as cutting the sandwich in half after: a more complicated way to reach the same result.

nodes.trait: A baked bun or roll, split, hinged or cut through
nodes.short: If the meatball sub is a sandwich, and everyone agrees it is, the hot dog comes with it. Same bread, different passenger.
Strictly, the genus of tube fillings. It keeps the name Canis for historical reasons, as real biologists keep a misnomer once it sticks.
A sandwich. The filling sits between two walls of bun, which is one more than an open-faced sandwich manages.
nodes.long: Merriam-Webster declared the hot dog a sandwich in 2016, and California and New York tax law agree. The National Hot Dog and Sausage Council disagrees, on the grounds that the hot dog has transcended sandwiches. The Review Board notes that transcending a category requires first belonging to it.

nodes.short: The food court legend: a quarter-pound hot dog and a 20-ounce soda for $1.50, a price unchanged since the mid-1980s. The price is part of the specimen. The flagship of the taxonomy.
nodes.long: Collected in the wild between the checkout lanes and the exit. Habitat: a metal table, never a chair. Diet of the observer: whatever was in the cart. The specimen is still ordered as "a hot dog," which is why it is a variety and not a species of its own. Diagnostic trait: the $1.50 price tag. Should the price ever change, this variety will be declared extinct and any successor described as a new variety. Since April 2026 a bottle of water may stand in for the soda; the Board considers this normal variation. Two Costco CEOs have been asked about the price on the record. Both said no, one more colorfully.

sources.title: Costco CEO promises the $1.50 hot dog isn't going away: 'The price will not change as long as I'm around'
sources.note: Fortune, via Yahoo Finance, March 2026. Current CEO Ron Vachris.

sources.title: Costco hot dogs have cost $1.50 since the 1980s. Here's why prices aren't changing
sources.note: NPR, June 2024. Includes co-founder and former CEO Jim Sinegal's warning to his successor about raising the price.

nodes.short: "Dragged through the garden" with mustard, relish, onion, tomato, pickle spear, sport peppers and celery salt on a poppy seed bun. Ketchup is grounds for deportation.
New York street cart classic. Unknowable flavor profile.
Wrapped in bacon and piled with beans and toppings. Pushes the variety rule to its limit.
Plain, or ketchup only. Included for completeness, not endorsed.

nodes.trait: A flat round filling: a patty
nodes.short: Burgers. Long accepted as sandwiches by people who reject the hot dog, which this genus finds awkward.
A sandwich. A whole bun, cut all the way through, holding a disc. Exactly as much a sandwich as the hot dog, which shares its family.
Spheres, in a roll, held in place mostly by sauce.
A sandwich nobody disputes, built exactly like a hot dog.
Chunks held together by mayonnaise, butter or optimism.
A hot dog bun with a better lawyer.
Cold cuts, folded and stacked in a roll.
Sheets of cold cuts in a whole roll. Still Integriformes when ordered as a 6-inch.
nodes.long: Subway bakes footlong rolls and cuts them in half to make 6-inch subs. The Board ruled that cutting a roll in half before building the sandwich is the same as cutting the sandwich in half after: a more complicated way to reach the same result. The 6-inch keeps its classification. It is noted here only as a terrible way of making it.

nodes.trait: A whole tortilla, folded or rolled
nodes.short: Griddled flatbread, so it is bread. The hot dog's next-door neighbors.

nodes.trait: A heap of filling: meat, beans, salsa
nodes.short: Whatever fits. How the tortilla closes over it decides the species: folded is a taco, rolled and sealed is a burrito.
A sandwich. Starch on the bottom and both sides, filling in the middle: the same shape as a hot dog bun.
nodes.long: A Massachusetts judge ruled in 2006 that one tortilla is not two slices of bread. A hot dog bun is also one piece, so that logic would expel hot dogs too. The Review Board declines to sacrifice the hot dog.

nodes.short: Fried, not baked. Still Formata: the phylum is about how the food is built, not how it is cooked.
Spit-roasted pork, pineapple and a folded tortilla. A sandwich.
Battered fish, cabbage and crema. A sandwich at the beach.
Fully wrapped, so it is more enclosed than a classic sandwich. A Massachusetts court disagreed in 2006; the court was not consulted on hot dogs.
The bread is fried on, in one piece. Still dough, still bread.
Tubes in batter. The genus name Canis was taken by the hot dog.
A hot dog fully swallowed by its own bun. The hot dog's cousin.

nodes.trait: A container of boiled or steamed dough
nodes.short: Sandwich architecture in a wet-cooked wrapper. A steamed bun is a dumpling, even when folded like a taco.
Pleated dough around a filling, steamed and pan-fried. The wrapper was cooked wet first, so it is a dumpling.
Boiled pasta sealed around a filling. A dumpling with an Italian passport.
A folded bao looks like a taco and is not one. The bun is steamed, not baked, so it is a dumpling.
The sandwich's cousin, not its sibling: the same architecture, but the container is rice, and rice is not bread.

nodes.trait: Pressed rice rolled fully around a filling
nodes.short: Cut a maki roll and the cross-section shows a container on every side with the filling in the middle. A burrito would recognize the shape, but not the material.
Not a sandwich. Pressed sushi rice encloses crab, avocado and cucumber on every side: sandwich architecture, but the container is rice, not bread. So it is sushi.
nodes.long: This ruling settled the question that started everything: what is bread? Bread is ground grain made into dough and baked, griddled or fried. Sushi rice keeps its grains whole, so however tightly it is pressed, it is not bread. The California roll is also an inside-out roll, with rice outside and seaweed within, which is why the rice, not the nori, is the container.

nodes.short: Pressed rice around a filling, often wrapped in nori. The rice is the container, so it is sushi in the broad sense.
Pastry above and below a filling. Not a sandwich, however hard the pot pie argues.
A stew sealed in pastry. The container decides, and pastry is not bread, so it is a pie.
A hand-held pie: pastry folded and sealed around a filling.

nodes.trait: A container that is a whole food (Naturalia), not a made material
nodes.short: Nice try.
A container, but not a dough-based one. A salad in disguise.
Shaped like a hot dog: a split container cradling a filling with condiments. Convergent evolution, not ancestry, because a banana is not bread.
Pizza, lasagna, nachos and cake. Where open-faced sandwiches go to think about what they did.
One face of bread is a topping arrangement, not a sandwich.
Not a sandwich. One slice is a topping arrangement. It stands or falls with thin-crust pizza, and nobody calls pizza a sandwich.
One base, toppings on top. Fold a slice, though, and it becomes a sandwich. Own it.
Not a sandwich. A pressed-rice base with fish on top: an open-faced sushi, in the same class as thin-crust pizza.
Lasagna and layer cake.
Layered, with no container. Not a sandwich, and the "is pasta bread?" fight never has to happen.
nodes.long: Lasagna has pasta above and below a filling, which looks like a sandwich until you notice there is no container: just flat layers, stacked. Pasta is also boiled dough, not baked, so the question of whether pasta is bread never has to be answered.

nodes.short: Soup, stew, ramen and cereal. The class level decides which of them are soup.

nodes.trait: Cooked together after assembly, or served in a broth simmered from ingredients
nodes.short: Soup. Either the solids and liquid were cooked together, or the liquid is a broth that was simmered from ingredients before they met. Serving it cold later is fine.
Soup by any definition.
Soup. In a bread bowl it gets complicated; appeals are pending.
Soup. Boiling water is poured over the dried noodles and seasoning, and they cook together in the cup after assembly.
nodes.long: The contrast with cereal is the whole point: cereal meets cold milk and nothing is cooked; cup noodles meet boiling water and cook in place. Same bowl-and-liquid shape, opposite verdict.

nodes.short: Soup. The noodles and broth cook separately and only meet in the bowl, but the broth was simmered from bones and aromatics for hours, and a simmered broth makes a soup.
nodes.long: Ramen forced the soup rule to grow up. Under the original rule (cooked together after assembly) it would not have been soup, and neither would pho. The Board added a second way in: a liquid that is itself a broth simmered from ingredients. Cereal still fails both tests, because milk is not a broth.

nodes.short: Soup. Rice noodles and raw beef meet a broth that simmered for hours; the broth clause covers it, and the hot broth finishes cooking the beef anyway.
Grain simmered in liquid, the same mechanism as chowder. Soup-adjacent, and the reason cold cereal is not.

nodes.trait: Never cooked together, and the liquid is not a broth
nodes.short: Solids in a liquid that was never a broth and never cooked with them. Not soup.

nodes.trait: Solids stay separate in the liquid
nodes.short: You can still pick the pieces out with a spoon.
Not soup. The flakes were toasted and the milk was pasteurized, but they were never cooked together. Not our problem.

nodes.trait: Raw solids blended into one liquid
nodes.short: Gazpacho, milkshakes and smoothies: blended cold, never cooked, and not soup.
Not soup. Traditional gazpacho is raw vegetables blended and served cold, never cooked. The rule holds even when it hurts.
Not a drink and not soup. Ice cream blended with milk is a dessert, and a dessert wearing a straw is still a dessert. Blended cold and never cooked, it shares an order with gazpacho.
Breakfast, so it is food, even through a straw. Fruit and yogurt blended cold: a close relative of gazpacho, and not soup.
Salad, fried rice and stir-fry.
Salad.
Romaine tossed with Caesar dressing, croutons and grilled chicken. Tossed raw, so it lives in Iactatae; the chicken was cooked first, separately, which does not count.
nodes.long: A useful test case: it contains a bread (croutons are Panes), a cooked meat and a condiment, yet it is not a sandwich, because nothing contains anything. It is architecture-free, which is the whole point of Mixta.

nodes.short: Stir-fry, fried rice and mixed casseroles: stirred together, then cooked as one.
Noodles, tuna and sauce stirred together and baked. Mixed, not layered, so it lives in Mixta.
nodes.long: Casserole is a pan, not a phylum. Casseroles are sorted by how they are built: layered ones, like lasagna or shepherd's pie, go to Stratifica; mixed ones, like this, go to Mixta.

nodes.short: A real biology term for organisms nobody can place. Ours holds candy corn, Jell-O salad and gas station sushi.
Under review since roughly 1880.
Contains elements of every phylum. The Board has recused itself.
